goal: Operate Watchdog as a secure, resilient, supportable professional SaaS product with governed Intelligence and server-authoritative access.

readiness_score.summary: Watchdog Intelligence Phases 1-8 are technically promoted and privately canary-accepted in production. The customer Account and Pro pricing surfaces now agree with the active Stripe Live catalog: Agent $59/month or $590/year, Pro $129/month or $1,290/year, and Pro+ $399/month or $3,990/year; Teams remains separately gated. Production Checkout v38 resolves prices by Stripe lookup key and validates exact USD amount, interval, active state and uniqueness while remaining fail-closed. Developer platform health v20 is Stripe-authoritative and validates a Live key plus all six lookup-key Prices without exposing credentials. Supabase leaked-password protection is intentionally deferred on the current Free plan until after at least 10 new users and is not a launch blocker. Remaining broad public paid-launch gates are direct production configuration of the Stripe Live key and webhook signing secret plus controlled real-money lifecycle evidence, and external legal/entity/insurance and operational alert-owner review.

phases.title: Trustworthy core
phases.focus: Server-owned authorization, sourced property data, mobile clarity and reviewed source health.

phases.title: Paid launch readiness
phases.focus: Two production Stripe secrets, controlled Live lifecycle evidence and final enrollment decision.

phases.title: Daily professional value
phases.focus: Change Intelligence, saved work, governed exports, evidence lineage and profession-first workflows are production-promoted while customer visibility remains controlled.

phases.title: Team operating system
phases.focus: Organizations, roles, jobs, usage controls, Daily Intelligence and governed team workflows are technically promoted; broad customer visibility remains gated.

phases.title: Resilient platform
phases.focus: Technical production promotion, private canary, cache/retry behavior, scheduler stop path and fail-closed Stripe launch code are accepted. Final real billing evidence and external legal/entity/insurance/alert-owner review remain; paid Supabase Auth hardening is deferred until after at least 10 new users.

items.detail: Production supports Standard, Agent, Pro, Pro+ and Teams as server-owned tiers. The Standard entitlement correction is promoted and verified against a real Standard production user: Standard is allowed, paid and unknown tiers remain denied. Paid-tier billing/plan mismatches are zero.

Stripe is the selected production provider. The active Live recurring catalog is Agent $59/month or $590/year, Pro $129/month or $1,290/year, and Pro+ $399/month or $3,990/year. Checkout v38 resolves the active environment Price through Stripe lookup keys with exact amount/interval/uniqueness validation; six historical STRIPE_PRICE_* variables are optional overrides rather than required setup. The remaining direct production secrets are STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET. After those are entered directly in Supabase, Checkout is placed in controlled mode for one explicitly approved real production account, the existing disabled Stripe webhook endpoint is enabled, and controlled real-money purchase, plan/cadence change, cancellation/reactivation where supported, payment failure/recovery, refund, replay/idempotency and signed-event entitlement reconciliation are required before public enrollment opens.

Stripe billing-price-catalog, Checkout v38, Portal and signed webhook implementations are promoted to production. The webhook includes atomic event claiming, stale-event rejection, plan/cadence/capacity normalization, invoice failure/recovery auditing and refund isolation. Production enrollment remains closed and the Live webhook remains disabled until the signing secret and controlled Live acceptance are complete.

items.capability: Stripe launch health and rollback control
items.detail: Developer Data Operations includes a private Stripe Live Release panel backed by get-platform-health v20. It reports only safe readiness booleans/counts, requires a Live Stripe key, validates 6/6 expected lookup-key Prices, shows Checkout mode, processed event count and lifecycle checks, and reads the server release gate. docs/stripe-live-acceptance-runbook.md defines controlled acceptance and emergency rollback. No secret value is exposed to the browser.

The full 43-migration production manifest is present and 23/23 allowlisted Intelligence Edge Functions are aligned to the accepted production bundles/auth modes. pg_net was added as the reviewed runtime dependency for the Vault-backed worker dispatcher. Production canary job 443fc535-5789-495e-8dcc-61680584cae0 resumed from a deliberately preserved fixture error to complete, processed one governed property, created one finding and run a8c40272-b199-402f-ab4b-6fad1de9410e using watchdog-population-worker-v3-governed-assessment-features. Cache probe c87cf0a6-9785-4a6d-96e9-9099a8426a03 returned cache_hit. Scheduler job 2 was disabled, verified inactive and re-enabled at the reviewed five-minute cadence. Customer visibility remains controlled.

Production authorization is server-owned, Access Boundary CI includes a billing-catalog consistency contract, and Security Advisor findings are classified against docs/property/security-definer-audit-2026-08-17.md. Anonymous public score/telemetry SECURITY DEFINER RPCs and authenticated owner/plan-gated RPCs are intentional API boundaries and are not blanket-revoked. Service/control tables with RLS and no client policy remain fail-closed by design. Leaked-password protection is intentionally deferred on the current Supabase Free plan and is not a launch blocker; revisit after at least 10 new users and a Supabase upgrade.

Access, sensitive workflow, billing, Intelligence and release-control evidence remain server-owned and auditable. Production access_audit_log tier constraints support Standard, Agent, Pro, Pro+, Teams and Developer effective-plan evidence so Agent billing events cannot fail after entitlement mutation.
All 15 production Advisor unindexed foreign-key findings were resolved with explicit covering indexes. A fresh advisor run reports zero unindexed-foreign-key warnings.

The governed 734-marker registry feeds canonical semantic snapshots with source state, freshness, missing/conflict preservation, facts hashes and versioned deterministic scenario lineage. Production Semantic Context/scenario/Analyst support functions are present on the accepted production bundles while customer visibility remains controlled.
Publisher/source monitoring and governed ingestion checks remain review-first and privacy bounded.
Bulk MOD-IV workflows validate and privacy-normalize source data; raw statewide work products remain outside the public application and publication stays explicit.
Sanitized client/service signals aggregate into private incident records; the public status endpoint exposes only broad component state and sanitized resolved timestamps.

NJW-42 isolated restore rehearsal passed with 112 public tables, 6 Auth users and 125 migration-history rows reconciled. Observed RPO was 0 minutes and observed RTO was 3 minutes. The operating objective remains RPO <=24h and RTO <=4h.

A GitHub-hosted public HTTP/content monitor checks the site root and Watchdog entry point on the default branch at the reviewed schedule. A human/operator still needs to own the external alert destination before broad public paid launch.

Terms, Privacy and Refund drafts have been updated to accurately describe Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, payment-data boundaries, cancellation and refund mechanics. They remain explicitly marked as drafts where applicable; external counsel review plus entity and E&O/technology-liability decisions are not being represented as complete by repository changes.

Account exposes server access state, profession personalization, support/status links and authenticated self-service JSON export. The plan grid now uses the correct Free / Agent / Pro / Pro+ / Teams ladder, syncs Agent/Pro/Pro+ display amounts from the Stripe-backed billing catalog with a verified fallback, and uses correct server tier keys. Stripe Checkout and Portal code are production-promoted while enrollment remains intentionally closed until Live billing acceptance passes.

Public Pro pricing and Account pricing agree with the active Stripe Live catalog. Checkout v38 resolves by environment lookup key, validates amount/interval/uniqueness, blocks Teams, blocks disposable Watchdog test accounts from Live spend, protects the legacy Paddle subscriber from double billing, and defaults closed. Agent/Pro public CTAs remain guarded until NJW-42 passes.
Disposable staging accounts and GitHub environment secrets exercise Standard, Agent, Pro, Pro+ and Developer authorization without production credentials.

Professional analysis, evidence review, governed population scopes, actions and lineage are production-promoted. A duplicate Data Workbench permissive RLS policy introduced by the Agent-tier follow-up was removed so the granular owner/team policies using can_use_data_workbench() remain the single authorization path.

The production population worker, one-time token dispatcher, resumable retry path, cache reuse and five-minute scheduler stop/restart control are directly evidenced in production. Broad customer visibility remains controlled.
Plan limits, job controls and Intelligence usage events are deployed server-side for the implemented Intelligence workflows; broad customer visibility remains controlled.

Organization/team schema and server boundaries are in production and the accepted Teams functions are deployed. Teams self-service enrollment remains closed until its separate commercial/public launch gates are satisfied.

Static access/security contracts, billing-catalog consistency, authenticated role gates and hosted Playwright acceptance are required release evidence. Coverage includes Dashboard, Home, Agent Control, Data Workbench, Intelligence admin, Account, Support and Status at desktop and mobile sizes.

Authenticated support submission uses function-owned Auth validation and the private support_requests store. Email fallback is available when sign-in is unavailable; operating posture uses an honest two-business-day acknowledgement target.
Account can download an allowlisted JSON export of the signed-in user's Watchdog profile/workspace/Intelligence records without cloning raw statewide data or payment credentials.

Privacy-safe Status and Support pages, status endpoint and operations/incident runbook are implemented. The remaining operational launch action is assigning/confirming the external alert owner/destination.

Fresh production advisor review is complete. All 15 unindexed foreign-key warnings, all per-row auth.uid() RLS init-plan warnings and the post-promotion duplicate Data Workbench permissive-policy warnings are resolved. Current Performance Advisor output contains only informational unused-index observations, intentionally retained until real production usage exists.
Versioned models, features, evidence, semantic snapshots, calibration and deprecation controls are in place; ongoing marker validation remains normal product operations.

After Watchdog has at least 10 new users, upgrade Supabase and enable leaked-password protection as a post-launch security hardening step. This is explicitly not a blocker for the initial Free-plan launch and is tracked in NJW-217.
Useful enhancement but not required for the technically accepted production platform.
Current responsive/focus/reduced-motion contracts are tested in core surfaces; a broader WCAG audit remains ongoing product quality work rather than a representation that formal certification exists.
Core product telemetry exists; final paid-funnel reporting should be validated against the accepted Live Stripe lifecycle before public enrollment.
Security answers, W-9/invoicing path and organization terms remain business-operations work before broad firm procurement.
